tooltip.title: Psoriasis as a Systemic Disease
tooltip.markdown: Psoriasis is not just a skin disease; it is a systemic inflammatory condition associated with numerous significant comorbidities. \[2, 7\]

tooltip.title: Psoriatic Arthritis (PsA)
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Prevalence:** The most common comorbidity, affecting up to 30% of patients with psoriasis. \[25\]
-   **Impact:** An inflammatory arthritis that can lead to irreversible joint damage and disability if not treated early.

tooltip.title: Cardiometabolic & Cardiovascular Disease
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Association:** Patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis have an increased risk of obesity, hypertension, dyslipidemia, type 2 diabetes, and metabolic syndrome. \[2, 5\]
-   **Mechanism:** Believed to be driven by shared systemic inflammatory pathways.
-   **Risk:** Leads to a higher risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), including myocardial infarction and stroke. \[7\]

tooltip.title: Psychosocial Comorbidities
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Conditions:** Increased prevalence of depression and anxiety.
-   **Impact:** The visible nature of the disease can lead to social stigmatization, low self-esteem, and a significantly reduced quality of life, comparable to other major chronic diseases like cancer and heart disease. \[2\]

tooltip.title: Other Associated Conditions
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Inflammatory Bowel Disease:** Increased risk of Crohn's disease.
-   **Uveitis:** Inflammation of the eye, particularly common in patients with PsA.
-   **Fatty Liver Disease:** Increased risk of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD).
